claims.text: Single-phase ZrB2 is typically produced at temperatures above 2300 °C.
ZrB2 has strong Zr–B and B–B interactions.
Single-phase ZrB2 has limited oxidation and liquid-metal corrosion resistance.
A controlled addition of silicon can form a ZrB2–xSix solid solution.
Silicon addition will enable ZrB2 densification at a sintering temperature around 1700 °C.
Incorporated silicon promotes mass transport during lower-temperature sintering.
Silicon doping reduces the activation barrier for sintering.
The enhanced lower-temperature densification produced by silicon improves structural integrity.
During oxidative service, silicon in the material preferentially oxidizes.
Preferential oxidation of silicon produces a thin silica-based surface layer.
The silica-based layer passivates the surface and reduces high-temperature oxidation.
The silica-based layer mitigates corrosion during exposure to a liquid plating metal.
Low-temperature Si-doped specimens will have greater densification than both high-temperature single-phase ZrB2 and previously reported lower-temperature specimens.
Greater densification in the Si-doped material will produce superior mechanical strength.
The Si-doped material will exhibit a lower oxidation rate than the stated comparison materials.
The Si-doped material will exhibit a lower liquid-metal corrosion rate than the stated comparison materials.
Previously reported lower-temperature undoped ZrB2 variants have inadequate oxidation durability and liquid-metal corrosion resistance.

contradictions.description: The design prepares only a high-temperature undoped control and a low-temperature Si-doped specimen, but the falsification rule also requires comparison against lower-temperature undoped samples that are not included in the stated design.
